puck-passing-point.alt: Top view of a level, frictionless table. A puck of mass m slides at constant velocity v along a straight dashed line. A point P lies off the line, a perpendicular distance d from it. The puck is shown at three positions; grey lines from P reach the first and third positions, and at the first one the angle θ between r and v is marked. The amber perpendicular from P to the line has length r⊥ = d. A panel gives L = rmv sin θ = mvd: r changes as the puck moves, but r sin θ always equals d, so the angular momentum about P is constant. About any point on the puck’s own line, L is zero.
